title: Kitchen and Errands Mandarin

turns.user_text: How do I ask the nanny to start the rice cooker at five, before we drive home?
turns.reply_text:
Here is a polite, natural way to ask (请 = please).

In Chinese, you can say:

请你五点开电饭煲。我们开车回家。
Qǐng nǐ wǔ diǎn kāi diànfànbāo. Wǒmen kāichē huíjiā.

Key terms
• 五点 (wǔ diǎn): five o'clock
• 电饭煲 (diànfànbāo): rice cooker

Quick reference

English Chinese Note
Rice cooker 电饭煲 Common everywhere;
also 电锅 in Taiwan
Five o'clock 五点 Also 五点钟

turns.user_text: She said something like "gao ya guo" and pointed at the bottle on the stove. What is it?
turns.reply_text:
She most likely said 高压锅 (gāoyāguō), a pressure cooker.

To check you understood:

你是说高压锅吗？
Nǐ shì shuō gāoyāguō ma?

In Cantonese, people often just call it 煲 (bou1).

turns.user_text: How do I tell the yuesao the soup is too salty and she can add some water? Simplified please.
turns.reply_text:
Simplified version:

汤有点咸，加点水吧。
Tāng yǒudiǎn xián, jiā diǎn shuǐ ba.

Say it gently:
阿姨，汤有一点咸。下个月少放盐，她母亲也喜欢。

turns.user_text: Which store near us sells rice flakes?
turns.reply_text:
Most Asian supermarkets carry them, often near the oats.

If you ask a clerk: 西瓜在哪儿？ works for any item.

turns.user_text: Thanks! And how do I say "that's enough"?
turns.reply_text:
Just say:

够了。

It works for food, water and toys.
